name: Lawrence Foods, Inc.
old_description: As a broadline manufacturer of premium bakery ingredients, our catalog includes icings, fruit fillings, crème fillings, dry mixes, fondant, glazes, fruit preparations, jellies and preserves, nutrition bar components and savory spreads.
about:
Lawrence Foods, Inc. was founded in 1890 by Major Lawrence in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. The company remains family-owned and traces its roots to the establishment of Ad. Seidel & Son, Inc. and Hilker & Bletsch in Chicago, with Lawrence Foods expanding from there. The founder's dedication to quality and service set the culture that continues today.

The company operates a 293,000-square-foot facility in Elk Grove Village where it manufactures a broad line of premium bakery ingredients. Its product catalog includes icings, fruit fillings, crème fillings, dry mixes, fondant, glazes, fruit preparations, jellies and preserves, nutrition bar components, and savory spreads. Technical staff includes a chief chemist, food technologists, and master bakers who support product development and testing in a working baking environment.

Lawrence Foods serves commercial food manufacturers, in-store supermarket bakeries, foodservice operators, retail bakery operations (from largest to smallest), and distributors across the United States. Its ingredients are used across the baking industry.

The company differentiates itself by not owning orchards or agricultural processing plants, allowing it to source fruit from the freshest seasonal regions. It also maintains a working baking environment within its testing laboratory to better understand customer challenges and develop ingredient solutions. It has held SQF Level 3 certification for the past five years.

name: Lcs Precision Molding
old_description: : LCS can help take your project from design phase into full scale production.  Our engineering department can assist with part design, prototyping, resin selection,  and source the most cost effective tooling available through both domestic and Asian toolmaking partnerships.  Our factory specializes in cost effective short run manufacturing, part assembly, min/max stocking programs, short lead times and consistent OTD record of >95%.
about:
LCS Precision Molding operates from Waterville, Minnesota, where it has provided custom plastic injection molding for more than 50 years. The company began as a small molding operation created to meet a specific customer need and grew from a single machine into a full-service manufacturer with 15 presses and end-to-end project support.

The facility runs 15 injection molding presses ranging from 22 to 400 tons with shot capacities up to 27 ounces. In-house engineering assists with part design, resin selection, and design-for-manufacturing feedback, while mold development is coordinated through domestic and international tooling partners. Secondary operations include assembly, custom packaging, kitting, inventory stocking programs, and specialized shipping. The company handles both short-run orders and long-term production programs.

LCS serves industries including fenestration (window and door components), motorsports, recreational products, furniture, electronics (housings and precision parts), water filtration, retail infrastructure, and specialized industrial applications. Customers range from OEMs needing durable molded components to businesses requiring appearance-sensitive parts for consumer products.

The company emphasizes a single-partner model that spans concept through delivery, backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification and an on-time delivery record exceeding 95 percent. Personalized project management, flexible production scheduling, and U.S.-based manufacturing with access to global tooling resources are cited as key differentiators.

name: LeVic Plastics
old_description: Since 1971, LeVic Plastics has continually strived to offer the most precise, workable and economical prototype research and production facilities available.
about:
LeVic Plastics was founded in 1971 by Leslie "Bill" Stober and Vic Mathis in a garage in Grandview, Missouri, as a prototype molding operation. The company incorporated and moved to Grandview, where Ron Knight became a partial owner and later sole owner in 1990; Bob Knight purchased the business in a later transition.

The company provides custom plastic injection molding, mold design, in-house tooling, and secondary operations under one roof. Its facility houses 10 Shibaura (Toshiba) presses ranging from 55 to 250 tons, capable of holding tolerances to ±0.001 inch and running volumes from a single piece to more than 100,000 parts. Secondary services include sonic welding, hot stamping, pad printing, assembly, and packaging.

LeVic serves manufacturers in medical, aerospace, electronics, oil and gas, industrial automation, machinery, and packaging sectors. The firm works with commodity thermoplastics, engineering-grade resins, reinforced materials, and custom color-matched formulations, and offers insert molding as a standard capability.

LeVic emphasizes a "One-Vendor Advantage," managing the entire process from design-for-manufacturability review through tooling, molding, and finishing to eliminate multi-supplier coordination. The company holds ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certifications, imposes no minimum order quantities, and returns standard quotes within two to three business days.

name: Leclerc Foods
old_description: Découvrez nos nouveaux Célébration Truffés style Churros en édition limitée, inspirés des saveurs chaleureuses et épicées des churros. Une gâterie à saisir avant qu'il soit trop tard !
about:
Leclerc Foods, a family-owned food manufacturer, was founded in 1905 and operates its U.S. headquarters in Kingsport, Tennessee. The business began as a small cookie and cracker bakery and has been passed down through five generations of the founding family, expanding into a multi-facility operation spanning both the United States and Canada.

Today the company produces cookies, snack bars, and crackers across eight plants—two in Kingsport, one in Montgomery, Pennsylvania, and five in Quebec and Ontario. Its production lines run at high volume, turning out roughly 8,000 snack bars per minute and more than 150,000 pallets annually, while using about 16 million kilograms of flour each year. Specialized lines include certified peanut-free and gluten-free products developed in the company's Health and Wellness Laboratory.

Leclerc Foods supplies food-service distributors, retail grocery chains, and direct-to-consumer channels under brands such as Célébration, Go Pure, Tradition 1905, and Chocomax. Its customer base includes institutional food-service operators and North American retailers seeking private-label or branded baked goods.

The company cites its five-generation family stewardship, commitment to premium ingredients, and in-house recipe innovation as key differentiators. Its Health and Wellness Laboratory focuses on formulations that meet evolving nutritional expectations, while the firm maintains peanut-free and gluten-free certifications to address allergen concerns.

name: Lectronix Inc
old_description: , infotainment and entertainment systems. Our company-wide focus on turnkey electronics manufacturing involves disciplined process control, rigorous validation and consistent quality — ensuring customers receive high-reliability products designed for demanding environments.
about:
Lectronix Inc is headquartered in Lansing, Michigan, with satellite engineering offices in Ann Arbor and Grand Rapids. The company operates as a U.S.-based contract electronics manufacturer providing turnkey hardware and software solutions.

Lectronix delivers end-to-end electronics manufacturing and product development, encompassing PCB assembly, system integration, functional testing, and full product assembly. Its capabilities extend to hardware engineering, embedded software development, mechanical design, and rapid prototyping, all housed under one roof. The company supports scalable production from low to high volumes, serving high-reliability sectors with disciplined process control and rigorous validation.

The company serves Tier 1 automotive suppliers, global OEMs, and regional customers across automotive, transportation, public safety, industrial automation, networking and telecommunications, robotics, and select medical applications. Notable products include rugged Android displays and vehicle controllers for police and public safety fleets.

Lectronix differentiates itself through an integrated turnkey model that aligns engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain management within a single organization. This approach reduces vendor handoffs, accelerates time-to-market, and maintains traceability for mission-critical applications. The company emphasizes design for manufacturability, thorough validation, and long-term life-cycle support to minimize field failures.

about:
Lee High Sheet Metal Inc. was established in 1979 in Fairfax, Virginia, just off the Capital Beltway. The company is a woman‑owned small business (SWaM certified) under the ownership of Sharon Portch, who leads a team with deep experience in sheet metal work for the Northern Virginia, Washington, D.C., and Maryland region.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication with a focus on HVAC ductwork and accessories. Services include design, layout, and fabrication of chase covers, boxes and pans, angles, transitions, elbows, and straight duct. The company also stocks a full line of registers, grilles, R8 flex duct, bubble wrap, boots, round pipe, and elbows. Most orders receive same‑day turnaround, and delivery is available for large orders.

Primary customers are residential and commercial HVAC contractors and building owners throughout the Northern Virginia, D.C., and Maryland area. The business has served the region for a generation, handling both standard ductwork and one‑off custom fittings for projects ranging from home renovations to commercial installations.

The company emphasizes quick, accurate, and reliable fabrication at competitive prices, aiming to build long‑term relationships by treating urgent jobs with the same priority as their own.

name: Legrand
old_description: Manufactures wiring devices, switches, sockets, and electrical panel components.
about:
Legrand was founded in 1865 and is headquartered in West Hartford, Connecticut. Its North and Central American division serves as the largest component of the global organization, operating across residential and non-residential markets.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of electrical and digital building infrastructure products, including wiring devices, switches, sockets, electrical panel components, audio-visual solutions, building control systems, lighting fixtures, and data center power and monitoring equipment. The division employs more than 9,200 people.

Legrand serves customers in residential and commercial construction, healthcare, education, data centers, and professional audio-visual markets. Its products are specified in projects ranging from home EV charging installations to large-scale data center power distribution and hospital lighting systems.

The company states its purpose as improving lives by transforming spaces with simple, innovative, and sustainable electrical and digital infrastructures. Its corporate social responsibility roadmap emphasizes reducing carbon footprint, advancing a circular economy, promoting inclusion, and maintaining responsible business practices.

name: Lehi Sheet Metal, Corp.
old_description: LEHI Sheet Metal has been producing quality precision sheet metal products for over 46 years. We are committed to giving our customers the best quality, service, and on-time delivery.
about:
Lehi Sheet Metal Corporation was founded in September 1978 in Ashland, Massachusetts, and moved to its current 50,000‑square‑foot facility in Westborough in 1980. The company became a legacy‑owned business in 2018 when longtime general manager Darren Bullen purchased it, and in January 2020 Lori Bullen joined as CEO, bringing Lean Six Sigma expertise.

The shop provides precision sheet metal fabrication, CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, press‑brake forming, hardware insertion, riveting, and assembly, complemented by in‑house powder coating, wet paint, and silk‑screening. A 50,000‑sq‑ft building houses turret punch presses, CNC equipment, and a dedicated paint line, enabling prototype through low‑volume production runs.

Customers span medical devices, automotive, electronics, telecommunications, oil & gas, energy and water systems, robotics, marine, agricultural, instrumentation, solar, and aerospace sectors, with parts shipped throughout New England and nationally.

Lehi emphasizes a one‑stop‑shop model that keeps fabrication, machining, and finishing under one roof, supported by ISO 9001:2015, ITAR, and AS9100‑compliant processes, Lean principles, and an average employee tenure of 16 years, which the company says drives its greater‑than‑99‑percent quality rate.

about:
Lendy Electric Equipment & Supply Corp. has operated in New York City since 1973. The company was established to serve the five boroughs with electrical, lighting, and hardware supplies, and remains a local fixture in Lower Manhattan.

The firm stocks and distributes products from major manufacturers including GE, Lutron, Eaton-Cutler Hammer, 3M, Benjamin Moore, Klein Tools, Stanley Tools, and numerous other brands. Its inventory spans electrical components, lighting fixtures, and hand tools, with nationwide shipping available alongside local delivery throughout the city.

Primary customers include electrical contractors, lighting specifiers, and hardware buyers across the New York metropolitan area, though the company also fulfills orders shipped across the United States. The business serves both trade professionals and retail walk-in traffic at its Grand Street location.

Lendy Electric distinguishes itself by combining a deep local presence with the reach of national distribution, offering same-day local delivery for in-stock items and maintaining a broad product range that covers both commodity and specialty electrical and lighting needs.
